blockers.description: modalApplyOneS5_spec : RuleApplicationSpec modalApplyOneS5 cannot be constructed. The rankStep field requires: for ANY rank : WorldIndex -> Nat satisfying (a) depth-bound hbound: forall x in b, modalDepth x.formula <= rank x.label, and (b) edge-decrement hedge: forall w w', acc.hasEdge w w' -> rank w' + 1 = rank w, the rule's output formulas satisfy the depth bound at a rank' agreeing with rank off the fresh point. Mechanized counterexample (S5Simplification.lean, section 'Phase 2 Obstruction'): Atom := Nat, phitest := diamond(diamond(atom 0)) (modalDepth = 2), sf0 := T(box phitest)@0, sf3 := T(atom 0)@3, branch := [sf0, sf3], acc := chain 0->1->2->3, rank w := 3 - w. hbound and hedge both hold at this instantiation (mechanically verified). modalApplyOneS5 sf0 branch acc emits T(phitest)@3 by rfl (world 3 is a known world of the branch, reached by the universal rule regardless of any edge to world 0). Since 3 != modalNextWorld branch (=4), any valid rank' is forced by rankStep's own 'agrees off the fresh point' clause to have rank' 3 = rank 3 = 0, but modalDepth phitest = 2 > 0. No valid rank' exists. Root cause: rankStep's K-style FMP rank-potential argument requires the target world's rank to be provably related to the trigger world's rank via a recorded edge (hedge) -- true for T's self-propagation and B's backward-edge propagation, false for S5's unrestricted propagation to every known branch world (which can include worlds in unrelated subtrees, e.g. created by unrelated diamond expansions, with no edge-relation to the trigger's rank budget). This is proven, not merely unproved: theorem modalApplyOneS5_rankStep_not_dischargeable is a complete, sorry-free, axiom-free proof of non-existence. Phases 4 (needs the spec for the generic Hintikka lift), 5 (needs spec.freshLocal), and 6 (needs 4+5) cannot proceed without either (a) a restricted S5 rule design that preserves rank-compatibility while still achieving full equivalence closure (not obviously possible, since EqvGen genuinely needs transitive reach across the whole known-world tree), or (b) a bespoke S5-specific termination argument that does not route through RuleApplicationSpec's rank-potential machinery at all (comparable in scope to S4/task 511's loop-checking problem).
